newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady, no rate rise speculation.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady, no rate rise speculation.

text.p: German call money rates were steady at Friday's levels of around 3.05/06 percent on Monday, with no speculation of interest rate rises in the market despite the strength of the dollar against the mark.

Dealers said that the market was very balanced at this level, although a full assessment of positions was made difficult by a delay in publication of Friday's data on reserve holdings at the central bank.
Data for Thursday showed banks held an average of 40.9 billion marks at the central bank over the first 10 days of the month.

Dealers said they expected the market to remain calm in coming days, with no major influences seen. At the same time, the market would continue to observe developments on the currency markets, traders said.

The dollar was trading at 1.7930 marks in mid-morning trade on Monday, not far below the 1.80 mark level which some have speculated may be a pain threshold for the German central bank, which signalled last week the dollar had risen far enough.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.07483 on Monday, up from 3.07400 on Friday.
